memo.verdict: Neutral; park; conviction medium at the Triaging stage. TotalEnergies (TTE-FR) at 74.46 EUR (2026-10-02) is a quality income compounder bought at the top of its own earnings cycle and is not compelling: the 'Modal return' is about 11.0 percent a year over eighteen months (to 2028-04-02; value including cash returns 87.08 EUR) and about 9.5 percent a year over three years (to 2029-10-02; 97.71 EUR) against the 20 percent bar. The park is not the gate's (management B, business quality B, predictability B, trackability B); it is the return's. Re-open on a price below about 62 EUR (the mid-point of the 57 to 66 EUR range at which the modal path clears the bar), or on two consecutive quarters of organic positive Integrated Power cash before farm-downs in the Q3 2026 to Q2 2027 prints, or on a cut to FY2027 consensus that puts the trough behind the price. A plausibly worse drop-through from EBITDA to EPS takes the return to F (5.4 percent and 6.9 percent a year) without changing the recommendation; the clearing price would then fall to about 52 EUR at three years.
case: The change is two changes braided together, and the market has paid for the wrong one. The company's own change is the next step of a six-year multi-energy build: EPH (14 GW flexible generation, €5.15 billion in shares, closed 29 April 2026), capital recycling at full speed (KKR €1.8 billion enterprise value, Shell onshore renewables, GIP $1.8 billion), 3 percent a year deepwater growth at $25 per barrel cash margin against $15 for the base, deleveraging to a 10 percent gearing target. The market's change is the Hormuz oil and distillate spike (Brent high $80s; European refining margins $13.50 per barrel in Q2 2026 against $4.70 in Q2 2025) that roughly doubled 2026 earnings against 2025.

The company's own change travelled the 'Six Layer Inputs-outputs' chain from choices and actions to the key operating metrics (power 14.8 TWh, up 28 percent; production 2.395 Mboe/d) and the financial statements (net debt down $3.34 billion to $19.71 billion). The sixth layer, the sell-side's estimates, moved far more (FY2026 EPS up 70.1 percent in twelve months) but on the oil price: the two house cuts after Q2 (Redburn, Jefferies, 4 percent each) were on the company's own lines, gas trading and production, while every raise came from refining margins and oil.

'Financial Outputs' surged and consensus has them receding: FY2026 11.80 USD to FY2027 10.60 USD to FY2028 9.74 USD. Our path (11.3, 10.0, 9.6, 10.2 USD) sits 2 to 6 percent below, on the company's $60 to $70 Brent planning range and no gas-trading recovery beyond normal. From the FY2026 peak the earnings compound at about minus 3 percent a year to FY2029; from the FY2028 trough about 5 percent a year (3.0 percent volume, 0.5 percent mix, minus 0.3 percent below EBITDA, 2.0 percent share count; the product 5.3 percent reconciles to the 5.1 percent claim). 'Goldilocks growth' F: above 40 percent over six months, negative over eighteen months and three years.
counter_case: TotalEnergies is the highest-quality European supermajor (Redburn), the only one with organic production growth to 2030, the lowest gearing (13.1 percent, heading to 10 percent) and the lowest unit cost (below $5 per barrel of oil equivalent), with a sector-leading free-cash-flow-per-share CAGR projected at 26 percent for 2025 to 2030 and a dividend that grows 5 percent a year through any cycle. It trades at 8.7 times against Shell's 10.0 and BP's 10.8 on the dashboard's P/E, at a 14 percent discount to supermajors on EV/DACF (Redburn), and at the 50th percentile of its own ten-year history while the peers sit at the 55th to 80th. The market gives nothing for an Integrated Power division that Morgan Stanley values at over $40 billion standalone by 2030 and the chief executive at a hypothetical $50 billion, which becomes net cash positive in 2027 and whose AI-driven trading the earnings review says could add 500 to 700 basis points of ROACE and $2 to $3 billion of annual operating cash flow by 2028. The consensus target of 88.39 (dashboard, 2026-10-04) plus the yield is about 24 percent in a year. Oil may not normalise: the Hormuz blockage has recurred (9 July 2026), OPEC+ is disciplined with seven members under-producing, Chinese export curbs and record-low diesel inventories keep cracks high, and non-OPEC supply declines below $60. The downside is bounded better than any peer's: dividend breakeven below $50 per barrel, organic breakeven below $26, a balance sheet that carries a $50 oil year without cutting the dividend. On that reading the case is a 'Compounder' mis-modelled on its Power line, the setup is B, the riskiness is the lowest in the sector, and D on the 'Investment Case' punishes the company for being large: every supermajor spans a hundred countries and five segments, and the thresholds of 20 countries and three Key Drivers were written for mid-caps. The return is B.

What the record concedes: the quality, every word; the discount to Shell and BP, which is real; the bounded downside; the Power optionality, for which the record puts 30 percent on the re-rating branch; the floor, with the fair trough moved to the five-year median (7.33 times) rather than the 25th percentile (6.57 times); the quality condition of 'Compounder' at B; that the E&P set flatters riskiness, which is why 'Riskiness' is C not D.
triggers: - Re-open triggers: a price below about 62 EUR (modal path clears the bar at 56.55 EUR at three years, 66.25 EUR at eighteen months; about 52 EUR at three years on the worse drop-through); two consecutive quarters of organic positive Integrated Power cash before farm-downs (would lift the re-rating odds toward even); a cut to FY2027 consensus that resets the cycle.

- What would change the view on each thing the case turns on: a Hormuz settlement that holds for two quarters with Brent still above $80 (the price is demand, not chokepoint); production below 2.35 Mboe/d for two consecutive prints; a buyback cut with Brent still above $65 (the cash engine weaker than the quarter showed).

- Alarm levels: Brent below $70 for a quarter; negative organic Power cash in Q3 or Q4 2026; production below 2.35 Mboe/d for two quarters; buyback cut below $1.5 billion a quarter; Hormuz curtailment back above 15 percent; a second consecutive Integrated LNG miss above 10 percent; a 5 percent FY2027 consensus cut over three months; the 24-month-forward multiple below 7.7 times; an OPEC fracture; breakeven above $30 per barrel; a contested May 2027 mandate vote; farm-downs at discounts to book; net revisions negative for three months; a flat dividend; an appellate confirmation of the vigilance ruling; direct sanctions on Yamal; the adjusted-to-statutory gap above $4 billion in a year.

- Invalidate levels: Brent below $60 sustained; negative organic Power cash beyond Q2 2027; production below 2.3 Mboe/d for two quarters with Hormuz eased; dividend growth below 5 percent a year; curtailment above 15 percent for four quarters; three consecutive Integrated LNG misses; a 15 percent FY2027 consensus cut over six months with the price unchanged; the multiple below 6.3 times with earnings unchanged; a binding Scope 3 order on upstream sanctions; an unplanned chief-executive departure.

- Dated steps: Q3 2026 results 2026-10-29 (gas trading promised back to over-performance; possible extra $1.0 billion Q4 buyback); Papua LNG FID by November 2026; Venus sanction; Mopane three-well appraisal H2 2026; gearing toward 10 percent by end-2026; Q4 results and 2027 guidance February 2027; Integrated Power net cash positive in 2027; Tilenga first oil 1H27; the May 2027 mandate renewal; Strategy and Outlook September 2027; EU Russian LNG ban and UK insurance ban from 2027 (negative); GranMorgu 2028; Mopane FID by 2028; Mozambique LNG first cargo 2029; Venus first oil around 2030.

- Gaps the record states: the framework's own track-record and lessons files and the Wisdom Library were not among the inputs ('No repeated errors' C as a gap); the live thematics file and the ticker's sidecar were not among the inputs; the dashboard's "consensus EPS now 9.255286" carried no unit and was not used; two production series exist under one label in the earnings review; Q2 2025 adjusted net income differs between two research sources by about 25 percent; FY2025 revenue differs between the risks research (USD 201,196 million) and the block (182,344 USDm); Eni's valuation letter differs between two dashboard tables.
